celaleyn:1-1.t: When it was revealed, he ﷺ said "Allahu akbar" at its end, so the takbīr at its end became a Sunna; and the command to do it at its close and at the close of every sūra after it has been narrated. It is "Allahu akbar," or "There is no god but Allah, and Allah is greatest." ﴿وَالضُّحَى﴾, that is, the beginning of the day, or all of it,

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا سَجَى﴾: covered with its darkness, or became still.

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿مَا وَدَّعَكَ﴾: left you, O Muhammad, ﴿رَبُّكَ وَمَا قَلَى﴾: hated you. This was revealed when the disbelievers said, when the revelation was delayed from him for fifteen days, "His Lord has left him and hates him."

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿وَلَلْآخِرَةُ خَيْرٌ لَكَ﴾, because of the honours in it for you, ﴿مِنَ الْأُولَى﴾: this world.

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿وَلَسَوْفَ يُعْطِيكَ رَبُّكَ﴾ in the Hereafter, of good things, an abundant gift, ﴿فَتَرْضَى﴾ with it. He ﷺ said: "Then I will not be content while a single one of my community is in the Fire." Up to here the answer to the oath (jawāb al-qasam) is completed, with two affirmative [statements] after two negative ones.

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿أَلَمْ يَجِدْكَ﴾: an interrogative of affirmation (istifhām taqrīr), that is, He found you ﴿يَتِيمًا﴾ through the loss of your father before your birth or after it, ﴿فَآوَى﴾ by bringing you into the care of your uncle Abū Ṭālib?

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿وَوَجَدَكَ ضَالًّا﴾ of the law that you now follow ﴿فَهَدَى﴾, that is, guided you to it,

celaleyn:8-8.t: ﴿وَوَجَدَكَ عَائِلًا﴾: poor ﴿فَأَغْنَى﴾: made you rich with what He made you content with, of war booty and other things. In the hadith: "Richness is not through an abundance of goods, but richness is richness of the soul."

celaleyn:9-9.t: ﴿فَأَمَّا الْيَتِيمَ فَلَا تَقْهَرْ﴾ by taking his wealth or otherwise,

celaleyn:10-10.t: ﴿وَأَمَّا السَّائِلَ فَلَا تَنْهَرْ﴾: rebuke him for his poverty,

celaleyn:11-11.t: ﴿وَأَمَّا بِنِعْمَةِ رَبِّكَ﴾ upon you, through prophethood and other things, ﴿فَحَدِّثْ﴾: tell. His ﷺ pronoun was dropped in some of the verbs in observance of the verse-endings (fawāṣil).
